sentences.text: 1  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.00.
Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgement and order passed by the learned HC-NIC Page 1 of 5 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:29:46 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/519/2008 JUDGMENT

Additional Sessions Judge, Morbi dated 23/4/2008 passed in Criminal Appeal No.2 of 2003, by which the learned appellate court has allowed the said appeal preferred by the original accused and has quashed and set aside the judgement and order of conviction and sentence imposed by the learned Judicial Magistrate (First Class), Vankaner in Criminal Case No.363 of 1987, by which the original accused was convicted for the offence under section 16B of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for short), the State has preferred the present Criminal Revision Application.

2.00. That the original accused was charged for the offence under section 7 of the Act alleging inter-alia that he was selling Mava without sugar, but it was found to be with sugar and therefore, it was alleged that he has committed offence under section 7 of the Act.

2.01. Before the learned trial court it was the specific case on behalf of the accused that the notice under section 13(2) of the Act, which according to the prosecution was sent to the petitioner, was, as such, not served upon the petitioner accused, and therefore, the accused did not get an opportunity to get the sample of the article of good analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory.

However, on the other hand, relying upon Ex.39, communication issued by the postal department, it was the case on behalf of the prosecution that the notice sent by registered post AD was served upon the accused.

Considering Ex.39 and despite the fact that the acknowledgment receipt of RP AD of notice was not produced on record, the learned trial court has believed that registered HC-NIC Page 2 of 5 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:29:46 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/519/2008 JUDGMENT post notice under section 13(2) of the Act, which was sent upon the accused, was served upon the accused.

That thereafter considering the material on record and report of the Laboratory and evidence of the Food Inspector,
the learned trial court convicted the accused for the offence under section 7 of the Act and convicted the accused for the offence under section 16 of the Act and sentenced the accused to undergo six months (it is not made clear by the learned trial court whether it would be RI or SI) and imposed fine of Rs.1000, in default, to undergo further SI for 30 days.

2.02. Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgement and order of conviction and sentence imposed by the learned trial court, the accused preferred an appeal before the learned Sessions Judge being Criminal Appeal No.2 of 2003 and by the impugned judgement and order and considering the fact that on the basis of Ex.39 it cannot be said that the registered post notice under section 13(2) of the Act was, in fact, served upon the accused and in absence of acknowledgment receipt of RP AD notice on record to prove that the notice under section 13(2) of the Act was served upon the accused, by giving benefit of doubt, the learned appellate court has acquitted the accused for the offence for which he was convicted by the learned trial court.
2.03.

Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgement and order passed by the learned appellate court acquitting the accused for the offence under section 7 of the Act, the State has preferred the present Criminal Revision Application.

R/CR.RA/519/2008 JUDGMENT
3.00. I have heard Ms.C.M. Shah, learned Addi Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the petitioner - State and Mr.Y.J. Patel, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent accused.
This court has considered the judgement and orders passed by both the courts below.
This Court has re- appreciated the entire evidence on record, more particularly Ex.39.

The short question which is required to be considered is whether the prosecution is successful in proving that the registered post notice under section 13(2) of the Act was, as such,
served upon the accused or not and therefore, whether can it be said that the accused was given an opportunity to request / get the sample of the article of the goods analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory as per sub-section (2) of section 13 of the Act or not.
3.01. At the outset, it is required to be noted that as such the registered post AD slip is not forthcoming and is not on record.
The prosecution only relied upon Ex.39 which is communication issued by the postal authority.
However, considering Ex.39, there is no reference to whom the said communication is addressed.
It also does not appear that the said communication is with respect to very registered post AD notice, which was alleged to have been sent to the accused.
Therefore, as such, the prosecution has failed to prove beyond doubt that the notice under section 13(2) of the Act was, in fact, served upon the accused.

3.02. Considering the aforesaid and by giving cogent reasons when the learned appellate court has acquitted the accused by giving benefits of doubt, the same is not required to be interfered with by this Court in exercise of the revisional HC-NIC Page 4 of 5 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:29:46 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/519/2008 JUDGMENT jurisdiction.

If the registered post AD notice under section 13(2) of the Act is not proved to have been served upon the accused, in that case, it can be said that the accused is deprived of its right conferred under sub-section (2) of section 13 of the Act.

3.03. Under the aforesaid circumstances, no interference of this court in exercise of revisional jurisdiction is called for and as such this Court confirms the findings recorded by the learned appellate court and consequent acquittal recorded by the learned appellate court.
4.00. In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, present Criminal Revision Application fails and the same deserves to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
